# launch_silolink_session_tool

> Launch a SiloLink session to explore, review, or modify code in a repository.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | `developer`, `silolink` |
| Callable | MCP clients; in-app @ai conversations; grantable to agents |
| Filter | `https://www.dsiloed.com/api/v1/mcp?tools=launch_silolink_session_tool` |

## Description

This is the description the server sends to the model, verbatim.

Launch a SiloLink session to explore, review, or modify code in a repository.
This creates a remote coding-agent conversation and sends your task to it.
The SiloLink daemon will automatically launch a coding-agent CLI session that
can browse files, search code, run tests, and make changes in the repository.

You can run the session on any of three coding-agent CLIs via `coding_agent`:
"claude" (Claude Code, the default), "gemini" (Gemini CLI), or "codex"
(OpenAI Codex CLI). Pick whichever fits the task; omit to use the daemon's
default (normally claude).

Use this when you need to:
- Review a codebase to understand its architecture
- Search for specific code patterns or files
- Run tests or build commands
- Implement code changes in a feature branch

The tool returns the conversation ID so you can check for results later
using conversation_chat_tool.

Launch verification: a success from this tool means the daemon CONFIRMED
a real tmux pane/session (status launched_verified), or the task was
delivered into a peek-verified live session (delivered_to_existing). A
failure (no_daemon / launch_failed) means NO session is running — treat
it as a hard failure, do not wait for results, and do not blindly retry;
surface the error. Only status 'launching' (legacy pre-1.19 daemons) is
unverified — confirm progress before assuming it is live.

Reporting pattern: the session reports back to YOU (the dispatching agent),
and YOU relay a clean summary to the end-user conversation. Set
report_to_conversation_id to your own working conversation (or omit it) —
never the end-user conversation — then post the outcome to the original
conversation yourself via agent_conversation_chat_tool. This keeps the raw
session log out of the human-facing thread.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session_name` | string | yes | Short identifier for this session (letters, numbers, hyphens only). Example: "architect-rate-limiting", "dev-task-101". |
| `task` | string | yes | The task for the Claude Code session to perform. Be specific about what to explore, review, or implement. Include repo path if known. |
| `repo_path` | string | no | Path to the repository on the local machine. Example: "/home/rholmes/projects/silo_link". |
| `report_to_conversation_id` | integer | no | Where the session posts its results when done. Set this to YOUR OWN working conversation — NOT the end-user/human conversation you were asked the task in. The session it @-mentions you there, which wakes you so YOU relay a clean summary to the end-user yourself (via agent_conversation_chat_tool). Pointing this at the human conversation dumps the raw session output there and is confusing. ENFORCED: if an agent sets this to the originating/human conversation it is dropped automatically (you are still woken to relay a clean summary). If omitted, results stay in the SiloLink session conversation. |
| `developer_agent_id` | integer | no | LlmAgent ID for the session to launch AS. Use this when a Dev Manager launches a session on behalf of a Developer agent — pass the Developer agent ID so the session gets the Developer persona and identity, not the Dev Manager. |
| `branch` | string | no | Git branch name for workspace isolation. When provided, SiloLink creates an isolated git worktree on this branch. Example: "feature/task-101-rate-limiter". |
| `base_branch` | string | no | Base branch to create the worktree from. Defaults to "development". Example: "main", "development". |
| `coding_agent` | string | no | Which coding-agent CLI the SiloLink session should run: "claude" (Claude Code), "gemini" (Gemini CLI), or "codex" (OpenAI Codex CLI). Omit to use the target daemon's configured default (normally claude). Set this when you specifically want a non-default provider for this session. One of: `claude`, `gemini`, `codex`. |
| `orchestration_execution_id` | integer | no | Orchestration execution ID — when set, the SiloLink session will be instructed to call remote_orchestration_stage_complete when done. |
| `orchestration_stage_execution_id` | integer | no | Orchestration stage execution ID — identifies which stage this session is executing. |
| `mcp_tool_allowlist` | array of string | no | EXTRA server tool names to make available to the spawned session, on top of the standard worker roster (data/admin/conversation/utility tools plus git_provider_tool, the orchestration tools, coordination_tool, org_lookup_tool and report_coding_session_usage_tool). This is ADDITIVE — you never need to restate the standard roster, and omitting this does not shrink it. Use it when your task instructs the session to call a tool outside that set, e.g. ["run_python_skill_tool"]. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | When true, return the would-be dispatch_conversation_id, sanitized report_to_conversation_id, workspace path (repo_path), and launch prompt WITHOUT calling Service::SilolinkLaunchService. Use this to preview a launch (eval scenarios, prompt regressions) without spawning tmux/Claude Code. Defaults to false; the response includes `dry_run: true` so callers can distinguish previewed launches from real ones. |
